name: 前景理论
oneLiner: 人对得失的判断基于参照点，且对损失比对收益敏感得多。
oneLinerEn: People judge gains and losses relative to a reference point, and losses loom far larger.
detail: 卡尼曼与特沃斯基发现，人们在收益区域倾向风险规避，在损失区域反而倾向冒险。价值函数以参照点为界呈 S 形，损失一侧更陡，收益一侧逐渐变平。这解释了为什么「先涨后跌」比「一直平稳」更让人难受。
detailEn: Kahneman and Tversky showed people are risk-averse over gains and risk-seeking over losses. The value function is S-shaped around a reference point, steeper for losses and flattening for gains — which explains why a rise followed by a fall feels worse than a flat path.
experiment: 抛硬币赌局中，实验对象普遍要求「赢了得 200 元才愿意冒输 100 元的险」，说明损失权重约为收益的 2 倍。
experimentEn: In coin-flip experiments, participants typically demanded a 200 gain to accept a 100 loss, implying roughly double weight on losses.
everyday: 促销说「立减 200」比「打九折」更打动人；因为前者被感知为收益，后者被感知为损失。
everydayEn: 'Save 200' converts better than '10% off', because one reads as a gain and the other as a smaller loss.

sources.label: 卡尼曼、特沃斯基《前景理论：风险决策分析》
sources.labelEn: Kahneman & Tversky, Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk

name: 锚定效应
oneLiner: 最先接触到的信息会像锚一样，把后续判断拉向它。
oneLinerEn: The first information encountered drags subsequent judgements towards it.
detail: 即使锚点完全随机、与问题无关，也会显著影响估计值。锚定之所以顽固，是因为人从锚点出发做「不充分的调整」，且倾向于搜寻支持锚点的证据。谈判、定价、估值都深受其影响。
detailEn: Even random, irrelevant anchors shift estimates materially. Anchoring persists because people adjust insufficiently from the anchor and tend to seek confirming evidence. Negotiations, pricing and valuations are all shaped by it.
experiment: 让被试转盘随机转到 10 或 65，再估计联合国中非洲国家占比：转到 10 的平均猜 25%，转到 65 的猜 45%。
experimentEn: After a wheel landed on 10 or 65, participants estimated the share of African countries in the UN at about 25% versus 45% respectively.
everyday: 商场先标「原价 1299，现价 599」，599 是否划算完全取决于那个被给定的锚。
everydayEn: A 'was 1299, now 599' tag makes 599 look cheap purely because of the supplied anchor.

sources.label: 特沃斯基、卡尼曼《判断中的锚定与调整》
sources.labelEn: Tversky & Kahneman, Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases

name: 损失厌恶
oneLiner: 失去 100 元的痛苦，需要赚到远超 100 元才能抵消。
oneLinerEn: Losing 100 hurts more than gaining 100 pleases, so gains must exceed losses to compensate.
detail: 损失厌恶是前景理论的核心参数，经验估计损失权重约为收益的 1.5–2.5 倍。它带来一系列可预测后果：不愿止损、过度投保、改革阻力大、以及「所有权带来更高的估值」。
detailEn: Loss aversion is the central parameter of prospect theory, empirically around 1.5–2.5 times gains. It produces predictable consequences: reluctance to realise losses, over-insurance, resistance to reform, and higher valuations for what one already owns.
experiment: 投资者对亏损头寸持有时间显著长于盈利头寸——「处置效应」，因为卖出即承认损失。
experimentEn: Investors hold losing positions notably longer than winners — the disposition effect — because selling makes the loss real.
everyday: 订阅自动续费取消按钮做得很深，因为失去已有服务比从未拥有更难接受。
everydayEn: Cancellation flows are deliberately buried: giving up an existing service is harder than never signing up.

name: 羊群效应
oneLiner: 跟随多数人行动，哪怕私人信息并不支持。
oneLinerEn: Following the crowd even when private information says otherwise.
detail: 当个体认为他人可能掌握更多信息时，模仿是理性的；但信息级联会把私人信号完全淹没，导致群体集体犯错。金融市场的追涨杀跌、消费潮流的快速形成、以及企业扎堆进入同一赛道都属于此。
detailEn: Imitating others can be rational if they might know more, but information cascades can swamp private signals and produce collective error — as in momentum trading, fast-moving consumer fads and firms piling into the same sector.
experiment: 阿希线段实验中，即使答案明显错误，只要多数人给出错误答案，约三分之一的被试也会选择从众。
experimentEn: In Asch's line experiment about a third of participants conformed to a clearly wrong majority answer.
everyday: 餐厅门口排长队并不代表更好吃，只代表前面有人排队。
everydayEn: A long restaurant queue signals earlier diners, not necessarily better food.

sources.label: 阿希《群体压力研究》
sources.labelEn: Asch, Studies of Independence and Conformity

name: 双曲贴现
oneLiner: 眼前的诱惑被过度放大，导致「今天说好、明天破功」。
oneLinerEn: Immediate rewards are over-weighted, producing plans today and broken promises tomorrow.
detail: 标准模型假设贴现率恒定，而实际行为表现为短期贴现率极高、长期迅速下降。这解释了拖延、存不下钱、健身计划半途而废，也说明「承诺机制」（自动储蓄、定期存款、惩罚条款）为何有效。
detailEn: Standard models assume a constant discount rate, but behaviourally the rate is very high for the near term and drops off quickly. This explains procrastination, undersaving and abandoned fitness plans, and why commitment devices — auto-enrolment, term deposits, penalties — work.
experiment: 多数人宁愿今天拿 100 元也不要一年后拿 120 元，却愿意在「一年后」与「一年零一天后」之间选择后者，显示偏好反转。
experimentEn: Many prefer 100 today over 120 in a year, yet choose 120 in a year and a day over 120 in a year: preference reversal.
everyday: 深夜下单、次日后悔；把购物 App 移出首页或设置 24 小时冷静期就是自我承诺。
everydayEn: Late-night purchases regretted next morning; removing shopping apps from the home screen or imposing a 24-hour rule is self-commitment.

sources.label: 塞勒、谢弗林《自我控制的困境》
sources.labelEn: Thaler & Shefrin, An Economic Theory of Self-Control

name: 心理账户
oneLiner: 同样的钱被分进不同「账户」，彼此不可替代。
oneLinerEn: The same money sits in separate mental accounts that are not interchangeable.
detail: 人们把收入按来源与用途分类：工资、奖金、彩票、红包各有不同花费规则。结果是同样的 100 元在不同账户中具有不同的边际消费倾向，也让「省下的钱」与「多赚的钱」在心理上不等价。
detailEn: People label money by source and purpose — salary, bonus, windfall, gift — and spend each by different rules. As a result, the same 100 has different marginal propensities to consume, and 'saved' money is not psychologically equal to 'earned' money.
experiment: 同一场演出，票是买的还是送的，退票率与再购意愿差异显著，尽管经济价值相同。
experimentEn: For the same show, whether a ticket was bought or gifted changes refund behaviour and willingness to rebuy, despite identical value.
everyday: 年终奖更容易被花掉，而每月工资则被小心规划。
everydayEn: Year-end bonuses are spent more freely than monthly salary, which tends to be budgeted carefully.

sources.label: 塞勒《心理账户与消费者选择》
sources.labelEn: Thaler, Mental Accounting and Consumer Choice

name: 禀赋效应
oneLiner: 一旦拥有，估值立刻上升。
oneLinerEn: Owning something immediately raises its perceived value.
detail: 经典实验中，随机拿到杯子的人平均要价约为未拿到者出价的两倍。它可以用损失厌恶解释：卖出被编码为损失。这也带来了「买卖价差」、免费试用转化率高、以及二手交易难以成交等现象。
detailEn: In classic experiments, randomly assigned mug owners asked about twice what non-owners offered. Loss aversion explains it: selling is coded as a loss. It also produces buy-sell spreads, high conversion from free trials and sluggish second-hand markets.
experiment: 康奈尔大学杯子实验中，卖家要价中位数 5.25 美元，买家出价中位数 2.25 美元。
experimentEn: In the Cornell mug experiment, median willingness to accept was $5.25 versus willingness to pay of $2.25.
everyday: 免费试用 30 天后退货率低于预期，因为「已经在用」使它变成要失去的东西。
everydayEn: Free-trial return rates are lower than expected: once in use, giving it back feels like a loss.

sources.label: 卡尼曼、尼奇、塞勒《禀赋效应的实验检验》
sources.labelEn: Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler, Experimental Tests of the Endowment Effect

name: 过度自信
oneLiner: 人们系统性高估自己的知识准确度、控制力与相对能力。
oneLinerEn: People systematically overestimate the accuracy of their knowledge, their control and their relative ability.
detail: 过度自信有三种表现：高估正确率（校准差）、高估控制力（错觉控制）与高估相对位置（多数人自认高于平均）。它驱动过度交易、创业热潮与项目预算超支，也会低估竞争与风险。适当自信推动行动，系统性过度则代价高昂。
detailEn: Overconfidence shows up as over-precision (poor calibration), over-placement (most rate themselves above average) and over-investment (illusion of control). It drives excessive trading, startup waves and cost overruns, while underweighting competition and risk. Healthy confidence spurs action; systematic overconfidence is costly.
experiment: 调查发现约 80% 的司机自认技术高于平均水平，这在数学上不可能。
experimentEn: Surveys find about 80% of drivers rate themselves above average—an arithmetic impossibility.
everyday: 频繁买卖基金的散户常跑输大盘，部分正是过度自信与交易成本所致。
everydayEn: Retail investors who trade often tend to underperform, partly due to overconfidence and costs.

sources.label: 巴伯、奥迪恩《过度交易》；摩尔—丹内尔「优于平均」效应
sources.labelEn: Barber & Odean, Trading Is Hazardous; Moore & Dunne, better-than-average

name: 框架效应
oneLiner: 同一事实换个表述方式，就能反转人的选择。
oneLinerEn: Rephrasing the same fact can flip people's choice.
detail: 当选项被描述为「存活率」还是「死亡率」、是「折扣」还是「加价」，人虽面对等价结果却做不同决定。这与损失厌恶和参照点有关：被框成损失时更愿冒险，被框成收益时更愿求稳。政策与营销的「选择架构」正利用框架改变行为。
detailEn: Whether an option is cast as a survival vs. mortality rate, or a discount vs. a surcharge, changes choices despite equivalent outcomes. Tied to loss aversion and reference points: framed as a loss people gamble, framed as a gain they play safe. Policy and marketing 'choice architecture' exploits framing to steer behavior.
experiment: 「亚洲疾病问题」中，把方案说成能救 200 人还是死 400 人，选择随之反转。
experimentEn: In the 'Asian disease problem', describing a plan as saving 200 vs. killing 400 flips the choice.
everyday: 「90% 成功率」听起来比「10% 失败率」更令人放心，尽管两者等价。
everydayEn: '90% success' feels safer than '10% failure' though they are identical.

sources.label: 特沃斯基、卡尼曼《框架效应研究》
sources.labelEn: Tversky & Kahneman, The Framing of Decisions

name: 现状偏好
oneLiner: 面对选择时，人偏爱维持现状，即便改变明显更有利。
oneLinerEn: When choosing, people prefer keeping things as they are, even when change clearly pays.
detail: 现状偏好源于损失厌恶、后悔规避与默认效应：改变被视为可能带来损失，因此需足够补偿才愿变动。它使养老金、医保等自动加入（opt-in）远少于自动默认（opt-out）参与，也让组织难以改革。默认值不是中性的，它默默决定了多数人的结果。
detailEn: Status-quo bias stems from loss aversion, regret avoidance and the default effect: change looks like a potential loss, so it needs large compensation to overcome. It makes opt-in far lower than opt-out for pensions and health plans, and stalls organizational reform. Defaults are not neutral—they quietly decide most outcomes.
experiment: 把器官捐献设为默认同意（可退出）的国家，登记率远高于需主动加入者。
experimentEn: Countries defaulting to organ donation (with opt-out) see far higher registration than opt-in ones.
everyday: 续订、套餐与隐私设置一旦设成默认，多数人一生都不会去改。
everydayEn: Renewals, plans and privacy defaults are rarely touched by most users once set.

sources.label: 萨缪尔森、泽克豪泽（1988）；约翰逊等《助推》
sources.labelEn: Samuelson & Zeckhauser (1988); Johnson et al., defaults

name: 公平与互惠
oneLiner: 人不只看自己所得，也在意分配是否公平，愿为惩罚不公付出代价。
oneLinerEn: People care not only about their own payoff but about fair splits, even paying to punish unfairness.
detail: 「最后通牒」「信任」「公共品」等实验显示，人会拒绝过低分配、回报信任、惩罚搭便车者，哪怕损及自身收益。这挑战了新古典的纯自利假设，说明合作建立在互惠、声誉与内在公平感之上，也为工资效率、税收遵从与制度设计提供依据。
detailEn: Ultimatum, trust and public-goods games show people reject low offers, repay trust and punish free-riders—even at a cost to themselves. This challenges pure-self-interest assumptions: cooperation rests on reciprocity, reputation and an innate sense of fairness, informing efficiency wages, tax compliance and institutional design.
experiment: 最后通牒博弈中，提议者开价过低常被拒，双方皆空手，只为「惩罚贪心」。
experimentEn: In the ultimatum game, a stingy offer is often rejected so both get nothing—purely to punish greed.
everyday: 商家「大数据杀熟」被发现时，消费者宁可弃用也要惩罚不公定价。
everydayEn: When price discrimination against loyal customers is exposed, people boycott to punish the unfairness.

sources.label: 古特、诺瓦布、萨缪尔森（1987）；费尔—施米特「利他惩罚」
sources.labelEn: Guth, Schmittou & Schwarze; Fehr & Schmidt, altruistic punishment
